1.q: Now Jehoshaphat had great riches and honor; he allied himself with Ahab
1.note: The word “now” is used here to mark background information. This happened before Ahab went down to Samaria.
Alternate translation: [he aligned himself with Ahab] or [he made himself a friend of Ahab]

2.q: Ahab killed many sheep and oxen for him and the people
2.note: This means that he had these animals slaughtered to prepare a feast for the people. Also, Ahab himself would not have prepared the animals, but rather would have commanded his workers to do it. Alternate translation: [Ahab commanded his workers to slaughter many sheep and oxen for a feast for Jehoshaphat and the people] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

3.q: Will you go with me to Ramoth Gilead
3.note: Here Ahab is requesting for Jehoshaphat to join him with his army to make war against Ramoth Gilead. This can be written explicitly. Also, in this question each of the kings represents themselves accompanied by their armies. Alternate translation: [Will you and your army go with my army to attack the city of Ramoth in the region of Gilead] (See also: [Synecdoche](ta:figs-synecdoche))

3.q: I am like you, and my people are like your people
3.note: Jehoshaphat is stating his allegiance to Ahab. Alternate translation: [I offer myself and my soldiers to you to use in any way you want]

5.note: Here about refers to himself accompanied by his army as himself. Alternate translation: [should we not]

5.q: will give it into the hand of the king
5.note: Here the king’s “hand” refers to his control. This means that God will enable them to defeat the people at Ramoth Gilead. Alternate translation: [will enable your army to defeat them] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

7.note: This is the name of a man.

10.note: This is the name of a man.
This is a reference to the horns of a bull but they made of metal.

10.q: you will push the Arameans until they are consumed
10.note: The prophet’s actions are a symbolic metaphor that illustrates the way that Ahab would defeat the Arameans. Ahab’s army will win with great strength, as a bull attacks another animal. Alternate translation: [With horns like these, your army will keep attacking the army of Aram like a bull attacks another animal, until you completely destroy them] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [until you consume them]

11.q: has given it into the hand of the king
11.note: Here the king’s “hand” refers to his control. This means that God will enable them to defeat the people at Ramoth Gilead. Alternate translation: [has allowed the king to capture it] or [will allow your armies to capture it] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

12.note: Translate this man’s name the same as in 2 Chronicles 17:7.
Alternate translation: [Listen] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you]

12.q: the words of the prophets with one mouth are favorable to the king
12.note: The prophets all saying the same thing is spoken of as if they all spoke with the same mouth. The phrase “the words of the prophets” represents the message that the prophets declare. Alternate translation: [the prophets all declare that good things will happen to the king]

13.note: “as surely as Yahweh is alive.” The people use this expression to show that what they say next is certainly true. This is a way of making a solemn promise. Alternate translation: [I solemnly swear]

14.note: The understood information may be supplied. Alternate translation: [or should we not go]
The word “we” refers to Ahab, Jehoshaphat, and their armies but not to Micaiah.

15.q: How many times must I require … in the name of Yahweh?
15.note: Ahab asks this question out of frustration to rebuke Micaiah. Alternate translation: [Many times I have required … in the name of Yahweh.]
Here the word “name” refers to authority. Alternate translation: [as the representative of Yahweh]

16.note: Here “all Israel” refers to the army of Israel. Alternate translation: [I saw the entire army of Israel]

16.q: like sheep who have no shepherd
16.note: The people of the army are compared to sheep that have no one to lead them because their shepherd, the king, has died.

Yahweh speaks of the king as if he were a shepherd. Just like a shepherd is responsible to care for and protect his sheep, the king is responsible to lead and protect his people. Alternate translation: [These people no longer have a leader]

17.q: Did I not tell you … but only disaster?
17.note: Ahab asks this question to emphasize that he had spoken the truth about Micaiah. Alternate translation: [I told you … but only disaster!]

18.q: on his right hand and on his left
18.note: This means that they were standing beside him on his left side and his right side. Alternate translation: [by his right side and by his left side]
This implies his left hand. Alternate translation: [on his left hand]

19.note: This means to attract someone by offering something appealing.
Ahab dying in battle is spoken of as if he will fall. Alternate translation: [die at Ramoth Gilead] (See also: [Euphemism](ta:figs-euphemism))

19.q: One said this and another that
19.note: This indicates that there was more than one opinion. The words “One … and another” refer to two or more angels in the heavenly host who were responding to Yahweh’s question in the previous verse.

21.q: become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets
21.note: Here the word “spirit” refers to the attitudes of the prophets and the words “the mouth” represents what they will say. Alternate translation: [cause all his prophets to speak lies]

22.note: Alternate translation: [Now pay attention, because what I am about to say is both true and important: Yahweh]

22.q: has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours
22.note: Here the word “spirit” refers to the attitudes of the prophets and the words “the mouth” represents what they will say. Alternate translation: [has caused your prophets to speak lies]

23.note: Translate this man’s name the same as in 2 Chronicles 18:10.

23.q: Which way did the Spirit of Yahweh take to go from me to speak to you?
23.note: Zedekiah asks this sarcastic question to insult and rebuke Micaiah. Alternate translation: [Do not think that Yahweh’s Spirit left me to speak to you!]

24.note: Alternate translation: [Listen] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you]

“you will know the answer to your question.” If Zedekiah’s rhetorical question is translated as a statement, this phrase may be translated to supply implicit information. Alternate translation: [you will know that the Spirit of Yahweh has spoken to me]

25.note: This is the name of a man.

27.note: This describes something that would not happen. Yahweh had already told Micaiah that the king would not return safely.

28.q: Ahab, the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went up against
28.note: Here the kings represent themselves accompanied by their armies. Alternate translation: [Ahab, the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah led their armies up against]
Translate the name of this place as you did in 2 Chronicles 18:2

29.note: This means to change the usual appearance so as not to be identified.

30.q: Do not attack the unimportant or the important soldiers
30.note: By mentioning both “the unimportant” and “the important soldiers,” the king meant all soldiers. Alternate translation: [Do not attack any of the soldiers]

31.q: That is the king of Israel
31.note: Jehoshaphat was wrongly identified as the king of Israel because Ahab had insisted that he wear kingly robes.

31.q: God turned them away from him
31.note: Alternate translation: [God caused them to stop pursuing him]
This phrase is used here to mark an important event in the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.

33.note: This could mean: (1) he took aim to shoot a soldier without knowing that it was Ahab or (2) he drew his bow to shoot without any specific target in mind.

33.q: between the joints of his armor
33.note: This is a place where two pieces of armor meet and is susceptible to arrows and swords.

34.q: the king of Israel was held up in his chariot
34.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone held the king of Israel up in his chariot]
